props.gloss_en: Beit Shammai: an Israelite is not counted with the priest for [eating] the firstborn
Beit Hillel permit [an Israelite to be counted for the firstborn]
even a gentile [may eat of the firstborn]
whose is the mishna? it is R' Akiva's
Beit Hillel: that [comparison to breast and thigh] is of an unblemished firstborn; of a blemished one it is written 'the impure and the pure alike shall eat it'
Beit Hillel: the impure may eat of a blemished firstborn -- 'the impure and the pure alike shall eat it'
and the other [tanna]? 'gazelle and hart' is written three times: one for R' Yitzchak's [teaching], one for R' Oshaya's, one for R' Elazar HaKappar's
as gazelle and hart are exempt from the firstborn [law], so disqualified consecrated animals are exempt from the firstborn [law]
Beit Shammai: a firstborn is not fed to menstruating women
Beit Hillel: it is fed to menstruating women
Beit Shammai: that [the impure eat the blemished firstborn] is where the impurity does not issue upon him from his body; where it issues from his body -- not
the mishna: a Pesach that comes in impurity -- zavim, metzora'im, zavot, niddot and yoldot do not eat of it
Beit Hillel: there the Merciful One revealed 'impure by a corpse'; here 'impure' is written unspecified -- there is no difference
one does not skin [an animal] from its feet on Yom Tov
likewise one does not skin a firstborn from its feet
nor disqualified consecrated animals
granted Yom Tov -- for he exerts himself with an exertion not fit for him [that day]
Rav Chisda: the firstborn clause is Beit Shammai's, who say it is not fed to menstruating women
Rav Chisda: the disqualified-consecrated clause is R' Elazar b'R' Shimon's
he had before him two sin offerings, one unblemished and one blemished -- the unblemished is offered, the blemished redeemed
the blemished one was slaughtered: if before the unblemished one's blood was sprinkled -- it is permitted
if after the unblemished one's blood was sprinkled -- it is forbidden
R' Elazar b'R' Shimon: even [when its] meat is in the pot [i.e. slaughtered before], and the unblemished one's blood is sprinkled -- it is forbidden
the mishna: all disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the market and weighed by the litra
evidently, since there is gain to the Temple, he permits it
Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana: what [skinning from the feet] improves in the hide, it damages in the meat
Ravina [as reported in the West]: because he appears as one doing work with consecrated animals
R' Yosei bar Avin: a decree, lest he raise flocks upon flocks from them
